chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام):
His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “But you prefer the life of this world.”
“And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.”
He (عليه السلام) said: “The wilayah of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام).”
“Indeed, this is surely in the earlier scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.”

key_terms.الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى: the earlier scriptures in which this truth is said to be found
key_terms.الْآخِرَةُ: the Hereafter, described as better and more lasting
key_terms.الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life, contrasted here with the higher enduring truth
key_terms.صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى: the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā, cited as earlier attestations
key_terms.وَلَايَةُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the wilayah of Amīr al-Muʾminīn, presented as the superior enduring reality
key_terms.وَلَايَتَهُمْ: their wilayah, identified here as the object being preferred

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) interpret “But you prefer the life of this world” in relation to wilayah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an interpretation of the verses by connecting preference for worldly life with accepting the wilayah of others, while what is better and more lasting is identified as the wilayah of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام). It frames this teaching as a truth rooted in the earlier revealed scriptures as well.
